# MCP tools

The tools of `odoo-work-cli mcp` ([how to connect a client](../how-to/85-mcp.md)).
Each tool runs the CLI command in the second column with `--json` and
returns its JSON unchanged: the fields are those of
[JSON output](20-json-output.md), a failure is a result with `isError: true`
and the [error envelope](30-errors.md). An argument is named like the flag,
with `_` for `-`.

The annotations tell the client what a tool does: `readOnlyHint` (changes
nothing), `destructiveHint` (may overwrite or remove data) and
`idempotentHint` (calling it again with the same arguments changes nothing
more). `odoo-work-cli mcp --read-only` serves only the read-only tools.

| Tool | Command | readOnlyHint | destructiveHint | idempotentHint |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [`whoami`](#whoami) | `whoami` | yes | no | yes |
| [`projects`](#projects) | `projects` | yes | no | yes |
| [`tasks`](#tasks) | `tasks` | yes | no | yes |
| [`entries`](#entries) | `entries` | yes | no | yes |
| [`timesheets`](#timesheets) | `timesheets` | yes | no | yes |
| [`clock_status`](#clock_status) | `clock status` | yes | no | yes |
| [`clock_list`](#clock_list) | `clock list` | yes | no | yes |
| [`entries_add`](#entries_add) | `entries add` | no | no | no |
| [`entries_update`](#entries_update) | `entries update` | no | yes | yes |
| [`entries_delete`](#entries_delete) | `entries delete` | no | yes | yes |
| [`clock_in`](#clock_in) | `clock in` | no | no | no |
| [`clock_out`](#clock_out) | `clock out` | no | no | no |
| [`clock_add`](#clock_add) | `clock add` | no | no | no |
| [`clock_edit`](#clock_edit) | `clock edit` | no | yes | yes |

Results over 32 KiB come in pages. The list tools take a `cursor`
argument: the second content item of a paged result says which page it is
and gives `next.cursor`; pass it unchanged, with the same other arguments,
for the next page.

## `whoami`

Current Odoo user

The Odoo user the server acts as: id, name, login, email, company. Same JSON as `odoo-work-cli whoami --json`.

No arguments.

## `projects`

List projects

Projects (with the configured filters), with id, name, customer, company, stage. Use search to find the project ID to book on. Same JSON as `odoo-work-cli projects --json`. A result over 32 KiB comes in pages: page and next are in the second content block; pass next.cursor as cursor, with the same other arguments, for the next page.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `cursor` | string | no | next.cursor from the second content block of the previous page of the same call; omit for the first page |
| `search` | string | no | only projects whose name or customer contains this text (case-insensitive) |

## `tasks`

List tasks

Tasks with id, name, project_id, project, stage; of one project with project_id. Same JSON as `odoo-work-cli tasks --json`. A result over 32 KiB comes in pages: page and next are in the second content block; pass next.cursor as cursor, with the same other arguments, for the next page.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `cursor` | string | no | next.cursor from the second content block of the previous page of the same call; omit for the first page |
| `project_id` | integer | no | only tasks of this project |
| `search` | string | no | only tasks whose name contains this text (case-insensitive) |

## `entries`

List timesheet entries

The user's timesheet entries of one week (default: the current one) or one date, with id, date, project, task, description, hours, status. Same JSON as `odoo-work-cli entries --json`. A result over 32 KiB comes in pages: page and next are in the second content block; pass next.cursor as cursor, with the same other arguments, for the next page.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `cursor` | string | no | next.cursor from the second content block of the previous page of the same call; omit for the first page |
| `week` | string | no | ISO week, e.g. 2026-W10 (default: the current week) |
| `date` | string | no | one day, YYYY-MM-DD (overrides week) |
| `project` | string | no | only entries whose project name contains this text (case-insensitive) |
| `task` | string | no | only entries whose task name contains this text (case-insensitive) |
| `status` | string | no | only entries with this validation status, e.g. draft or validated |

## `timesheets`

Weekly timesheet

All timesheet entries of one ISO week (default: the current one). Same JSON as `odoo-work-cli timesheets --json`. A result over 32 KiB comes in pages: page and next are in the second content block; pass next.cursor as cursor, with the same other arguments, for the next page.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `cursor` | string | no | next.cursor from the second content block of the previous page of the same call; omit for the first page |
| `week` | string | no | ISO week, e.g. 2026-W10 (default: the current week) |

## `clock_status`

Attendance status

Whether the user is clocked in, since when, and today's attendance periods and total. Same JSON as `odoo-work-cli clock status --json`.

No arguments.

## `clock_list`

List attendance records

Attendance records of one day (default today) or one ISO week, with id, check_in, check_out, running, worked_hours. Same JSON as `odoo-work-cli clock list --json`. A result over 32 KiB comes in pages: page and next are in the second content block; pass next.cursor as cursor, with the same other arguments, for the next page.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `cursor` | string | no | next.cursor from the second content block of the previous page of the same call; omit for the first page |
| `date` | string | no | the day, YYYY-MM-DD (default today); not together with week |
| `week` | string | no | an ISO week, e.g. 2026-W10; not together with date |

## `entries_add`

Book a timesheet entry

Create a timesheet entry and return it. With dry_run=true nothing is written: the entry that would be created comes back with dry_run true and the duplicates (same day, project, task and description). Propose with dry_run first. Same JSON as `odoo-work-cli entries add --json`.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `project_id` | integer | yes | project ID (from projects) |
| `task_id` | integer | no | task ID of that project (from tasks) |
| `date` | string | no | YYYY-MM-DD (default today) |
| `hours` | number or string | yes | hours worked: a number (2.5) or H:MM ("2:30") |
| `description` | string | yes | what was done |
| `dry_run` | boolean | no | resolve and validate, print the entry that would be written and its duplicates, write nothing |

## `entries_update`

Change a timesheet entry

Overwrite the given fields of a timesheet entry and return it; fields not given stay. With dry_run=true nothing is written: the merged entry comes back with dry_run true. Same JSON as `odoo-work-cli entries update --json`.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | integer | yes | entry ID (from entries) |
| `project_id` | integer | no | new project ID |
| `task_id` | integer | no | new task ID |
| `date` | string | no | new date, YYYY-MM-DD |
| `hours` | number or string | no | hours worked: a number (2.5) or H:MM ("2:30") |
| `description` | string | no | new description |
| `dry_run` | boolean | no | resolve and validate, print the entry that would be written and its duplicates, write nothing |

## `entries_delete`

Delete a timesheet entry

Delete a timesheet entry and return it as it was. Same JSON as `odoo-work-cli entries delete --json`.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | integer | yes | entry ID (from entries) |

## `clock_in`

Clock in

Start attendance now (or at a past time) and return the running record. conflict when already clocked in. Same JSON as `odoo-work-cli clock in --json`.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `at` | string | no | a past time (HH:MM or YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM) instead of now; needs attendance officer rights |

## `clock_out`

Clock out

End the running attendance now (or at a past time) and return the record. conflict when not clocked in. Same JSON as `odoo-work-cli clock out --json`.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `at` | string | no | a past time (HH:MM or YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM) instead of now; needs attendance officer rights |

## `clock_add`

Add an attendance record

Create one attendance record with check-in and check-out, for several records a day (e.g. around a break). conflict, and nothing written, when it overlaps a record. Same JSON as `odoo-work-cli clock add --json`.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `date` | string | no | the day, YYYY-MM-DD (default today) |
| `in` | string | yes | check-in, HH:MM or YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM |
| `out` | string | yes | check-out, HH:MM or YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (a later day for overnight) |

## `clock_edit`

Set a day's attendance

Set check-in and/or check-out of the day's attendance record, or create it when the day has none; returns before and after. Overwrites an existing record unless create_only. Same JSON as `odoo-work-cli clock edit --json`.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `date` | string | no | the day, YYYY-MM-DD (default today) |
| `in` | string | no | new check-in, HH:MM or YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM |
| `out` | string | no | new check-out, HH:MM or YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM |
| `id` | integer | no | the record to edit when the day has several (from clock_list) |
| `create_only` | boolean | no | only create; conflict, and nothing changed, when the day already has a record |
